question.problem:
Given the joint probability distribution for two discrete random variables $X$ and $Y$ below, find $\text{E}[6X+Y].$

| $f$ | $Y=1$ | $Y=3$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $X=-1$ | $0.35$ | $0.1$ |
| $X=1$ | $0.25$ | $0.3$ |
question.worked_solution:
Recall that the marginal distribution for $X$ corresponds to the row totals, and the marginal distribution for $Y$ corresponds to the column totals. | $f$ | $Y=1$ | $Y=3$ | ${f}_{X}$ | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | $X=-1$ | $0.35$ | $0.1$ | $0.45$ | | $X=1$ | $0.25$ | $0.3$ | $0.55$ | | ${f}_{Y}$ | $0.6$ | $0.4$ | $1$ | Therefore, the probability mass functions for $X$ and $Y$ are given by the following tables:
$x$ $-1$ $1$
${f}_{X}(x)$ $0.45$ $0.55$

$y$ $1$ $3$
${f}_{Y}(y)$ $0.6$ $0.4$

Now, we can compute the expected values for $X$ and $Y:$ $$ \begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}\,{f}_{X}({x}_{i}) \\ & =(-1)\cdot 0.45+1\cdot 0.55 \\ & =-0.45+0.55 \\ & =0.1.\end{aligned} $$ $$ \begin{aligned}\text{E}[Y] & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{y}_{i}\,{f}_{Y}({y}_{i}) \\ & =1\cdot 0.6+3\cdot 0.4 \\ & =0.6+1.2 \\ & =1.8.\end{aligned} $$ Finally, using the properties of expectation, we obtain $$ \begin{aligned}\text{E}[6X+Y] & =6\,\text{E}[X]+\,\text{E}[Y] \\ & =6(0.1)+1.8 \\ & =0.6+1.8 \\ & =2.4.\end{aligned} $$
